title: Formal monoid completion over the completed regular Laurent stratum
statement:
Let $L$ be a field or a Cohen ring [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_L$, let $K$ be a finite free abelian group, let $T$ be a sharp fine saturated additive monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], sharp meaning that $0$ is its only invertible element, and let $n\ge0$. Put $E=L[K][t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, choose any prime $\mathfrak p\subset E$ containing $(\mathfrak m_L,t_1,\ldots,t_n)$, and set
$$E_*=E_{\mathfrak p},\quad D=\widehat {E_*},\quad U=E[T],\quad\mathfrak r=\mathfrak pU+([v]:v\in T\setminus\{0\}),\quad Z=U_{\mathfrak r}.$$
Localizations and maximal-ideal completions use [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Monoid rings $E[M]$ consist of finite sums $\sum c_u[u]$ with $[u][v]=[u+v]$.
Then $D$ is a nonzero complete regular Noetherian local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with residue field $\operatorname{Frac}(E/\mathfrak p)$. Write
$$\mathfrak b=(\mathfrak m_{E_*},[v]:v\ne0)E_*[T],\quad\mathfrak a=(\mathfrak m_D,[v]:v\ne0)D[T],\quad H=D[[T]]=\varprojlim_jD[T]/\mathfrak a^j.$$
The canonical maps induce compatible isomorphisms for all $j\ge1$,
$$Z/\mathfrak m_Z^j\cong E_*[T]/\mathfrak b^j\cong D[T]/\mathfrak a^j,$$
and hence a continuous isomorphism $\widehat Z\cong H$ with continuous inverse, sending every coefficient $e\in E$ to its image in $D$ and every $[v]$ to $[v]$. Moreover $H/([v]:v\ne0)H\cong D$, by the coefficient map and the augmentation killing the nonzero $T$-monomials. The construction allows $T=\{0\}$, $K=0$, and $n=0$.

source.place: VI 1.6, printed p. 70; agent-supplied construction of the coefficient stratum before its relation and calculation of all monomial-adic quotients, returned proof Steps 9--10 and the augmentation identification in Step 13.

proof.text: The zero-variable case of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] makes $L$ regular local, for either allowed kind of coefficient ring. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization] it is a regular ring. Choose a basis of $K$ of size $h$. The assignments $x_i\mapsto[e_i]$, $x_i^{-1}\mapsto[-e_i]$ identify $E$ with $L[x_1,\ldots,x_h,t_1,\ldots,t_n][(x_1\cdots x_h)^{-1}]$: the inverse sends $[\sum a_ie_i]t^b$ to $x^at^b$, extended coefficientwise. For $h=0$ the product is $1$. Apply [lem-trf-polynomial-ring-regular-base] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-regular-ring] to this presentation. Thus $E$ is Noetherian and regular; its prime localization $A=E_*$ is regular local by the definition [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Tags 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary), zero variables; 0AFS (lemma-localization-of-regular-local-is-regular); regular polynomial input is the cited Mathlib leaf. Laurent presentation is explicit agent algebra.

proof.text: Write $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_A$. Since $A$ is Noetherian local, [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local] and [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] make $D$ regular and Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], $\mathfrak m_D=\mathfrak mD$ and $D/\mathfrak m_D\cong A/\mathfrak m$. Completeness for $\mathfrak mD$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal], since $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated. The fraction description [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] gives $A/\mathfrak m\cong\operatorname{Frac}(E/\mathfrak p)$: $e/s\mapsto\bar e/\bar s$; every nonzero class of $E/\mathfrak p$ is an allowed denominator, and the fraction equality is the same after reduction. This is a nonzero field, so its surjective preimage $D$ is nonzero.

Apply [lem-trf-sharp-fs-orthant-embedding] to $T$. Identify it with its image $P\subseteq\mathbf N^r\subseteq\mathbf Z^r$; take $w(a)=\sum_i a_i$. Injectivity makes $w$ strictly positive away from zero. This supplies precisely the ambient free group and positive weight required below, without any freeness assumption on $T$ itself. Choose a finite generating list of $T$ and omit its zero entries. The corresponding nonzero monomials generate the whole nonzero-monomial ideal: a nonzero exponent is a sum of generators and hence has a nonzero generator as a summand. In particular $U=E[T]$ and $B=A[T]$ are finite type algebras. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] they are Noetherian; [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] makes $Z$ Noetherian. The same argument gives that $D[T]$ is Noetherian. All ideals used for completions are therefore finitely generated.

source.place: VI 1.6, printed p. 70, agent construction; orthant input is the cited DAG statement; Noetherian input: Stacks algebra.tex Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence).

proof.text: Sharpness implies that a sum of two exponents is zero only when both are zero, so augmentation $U\to E$ is a ring map. Its composite with $E\to E/\mathfrak p$ has kernel exactly $\mathfrak r$; hence $\mathfrak r$ is prime. A polynomial lies outside $\mathfrak r$ exactly when its constant coefficient is outside $\mathfrak p$. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $Z$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak rZ$. Every $s\in E\setminus\mathfrak p$ is invertible in $Z$, so $B=A[T]\to Z$ is defined by $[v]\mapsto[v]$ and $e/s\mapsto(e/1)(s/1)^{-1}$. Its coefficient maximal ideal is generated by fractions $e/s$ with $e\in\mathfrak p$, and therefore $\mathfrak bZ=\mathfrak rZ=\mathfrak m_Z$. This defines the canonical map $B/\mathfrak b^j\to Z/\mathfrak m_Z^j$ for every $j\ge1$.

source.place: VI 1.6, printed p. 70: agent-supplied augmentation and localization calculation.

proof.text:
For $s\in U\setminus\mathfrak r$, its image in $B$ is $c+h$, with $c\in A^\times$ its constant coefficient and $h$ in the nonzero-monomial ideal. In $B/\mathfrak b^j$, $h^j=0$, and an inverse of $s$ is
$$c^{-1}\sum_{i=0}^{j-1}(-c^{-1}h)^i.$$
Indeed multiplication gives $1-(-c^{-1}h)^j=1$. Define $Z\to B/\mathfrak b^j$ by $u/s\mapsto\bar u\bar s^{-1}$. The equality of fractions in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] proves well-definedness: a cross-product difference annihilated by some element outside $\mathfrak r$ maps to zero because that annihilator maps to a unit. The map kills $\mathfrak m_Z^j$ since it sends every generator of $\mathfrak rZ$ into $\mathfrak b/\mathfrak b^j$. It is inverse to the map of Step 4: both composites fix coefficients and monomials, and a homomorphism fixing an invertible element fixes its inverse. Thus $Z/\mathfrak m_Z^j\cong B/\mathfrak b^j$. These maps commute with reduction: they all extend the same map from $U$, and send each denominator to the unique inverse of its image.

source.place: VI 1.6, printed p. 70: agent-supplied finite nilpotent geometric-series inverse; no assertion of this Laurent comparison is attributed to ILO.

proof.text:
Use [lem-trf-positive-monoid-adic-filtration] with $P$ from Step 3, first over $A$ with ideal $\mathfrak m$, and then over $D$ with ideal $\mathfrak m_D$. It gives a finite set $S_j=\{v:
u(v)<j\}$ and identifies the coefficient modules of the two quotients as
$$B/\mathfrak b^j= igoplus_{v\in S_j} A/\mathfrak m^{j-
u(v)},\qquad D[T]/\mathfrak a^j= igoplus_{v\in S_j}D/\mathfrak m_D^{j-
u(v)}.$$
Here equality denotes the canonical additive coefficient identification supplied by the ideal-membership formula: monomials outside $S_j$ vanish, and coefficients at $v\in S_j$ are reduced by exactly that power. Since $\mathfrak m_D=\mathfrak mD$, [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] identifies each pair of summands via $A	o D$. Thus the canonical ring map $B/\mathfrak b^j	o D[T]/\mathfrak a^j$ is bijective. It is already a ring map, since it applies $A	o D$ coefficientwise and preserves monomials. Both quotient maps at $j+1$ and $j$ are induced by that single ring map, so their squares with reduction commute.

source.place: VI 1.6, printed p. 70: agent coefficient calculation from the cited filtration statement; coefficient completion input: Stacks algebra.tex Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated).

proof.text: Compose the isomorphisms of Steps 5--6 to obtain $e_j:Z/\mathfrak m_Z^j\cong D[T]/\mathfrak a^j$. Their reduction compatibility permits [lem-trf-adic-inverse-limit-iso], giving $\widehat Z\cong H$. It sends the tuple for $e\in E$ to the tuple of its image in $D$ and fixes the tuple of every $[v]$, because every $e_j$ does. For every $j$, the isomorphism takes the kernel of the $j$th projection onto the kernel of the $j$th projection. These are the respective $j$th powers of the extended defining ideals by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power], applied to the finitely generated ideals $\mathfrak m_Z$ and $\mathfrak a$ (Step 3). Hence both the map and its inverse are continuous for the adic topologies.

source.place: Tags 00M9 (section-completion), compatible sequences, and 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), projection kernels.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-formal-monoid-residue-domain] with coefficient ring $D$, monoid $P$ and weight $w$. Step 2 supplies a nonzero complete separated Noetherian local coefficient ring, and Step 3 supplies the finitely generated submonoid of a finite rank free group and strict positivity. Its completion is exactly $H$. Its stated constant-coefficient homomorphism has kernel $([v]:v
e0)H$ and induces $H/([v]:v
e0)H\cong D$, with inverse given by coefficients. All constructions allow an empty list of nonzero monoid generators: for $T=\{0\}$ the filtration has $
u(0)=0$, the sole summand in Step 6 is $A/\mathfrak m^j$, and the last assertion identifies $H=D$. Empty Laurent and polynomial variable lists were allowed in Step 1, so $K=0$ and $n=0$, separately or simultaneously, require no additional hypothesis.
